recorded.final_text:
If you've lost a UVA Library book, here's what to do:

*1. Contact/check first*
• If it's overdue and not yet billed, try to locate/return it as soon as possible to avoid a replacement charge.
• If it's already significantly overdue, the Library will bill you for the replacement cost and suspend your borrowing privileges (including Special Collections, Interlibrary Loan, and LEO delivery) until it's resolved.

*2. Paying the bill*
• *Students*: Fines/bills go through Student Financial Services and appear in your SIS account (7–10 days after billing). Students can only pay through SIS.
• *Non-students*: Pay online with a credit/debit card, or in person at Shannon Library with exact cash or personal check (no in-person card payments).

*3. Good news if you find it later*
• If you later find and return the book, the bill can be removed — as long as it's returned within *90 days* of payment and the item isn't damaged.

*4. Questions about a specific bill or item*
• Contact Access Services / Circulation directly for details about your specific charge.

📄 Full policy details: <https://library.virginia.edu/policies/circulation/|UVA Library Circulation Policy>

If the lost item was borrowed via Interlibrary Loan (from another library, not UVA's own collection), the process is a bit different — let me know and I can pull up those specifics too.
